To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dual remote sensing (RS)-technique is more accurate in detecting high-emitting vehicles than the single RS technique, while both techniques show the same accuracy in estimating average emission factors when a sufficient number of RS measurements are available.
The dual RS technique is a promising method for identifying high-emitting in-use vehicles and improving the accuracy of on-road vehicle emission estimation.

using the single remote sensing technique may be insufficient for accurately representing the emission level of vehicles based on a single measurement; the dual remote sensing technique is more effective in identifying high-emitting vehicle; both remote sensing systems demonstrate the same gamma distribution and converged mean emission factors when a large number (>200) number of measurements are obtained; and the minimum sample size of remote sensing measurements is 200 for generating reliable emission factors of on-road vehicles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the statistical characteristics of on-road emissions and provides useful insights to improve the accuracy of on-road emissions measurement.
the development of a dual RS technique to measure the emissions of inuse vehicles on-road and to assess their characteristics under realworld driving conditions.
the statistical analysis of the emission measurement results from two RS systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dual RS technique should be used for the purpose of identifying high-emitters, and the single RS technique should be applied for the purpose of calculating the average emissions of a vehicle group.
the dual RS technique can provide more accurate information on vehicle emissions, but the sample size needs to be large enough.

both the single and dual remote sensing techniques are equally valid in terms of their emission factor estimates when sufficient data are available, while only the dual remote sensing technique is valid in terms of identifying high-emission vehicles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a dual RS system can improve the accuracy of identifying in-use vehicles with high emissions, which can be used for emission control programs.
the dual RS system is a more accurate and effective method than a single system to monitor on-road vehicle emissions.

the single RS technique can be applied in large-scale monitoring and control programs, whereas the dual RS technique should be applied in emission inventory development and emission control strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single RS measurement is insufficient to accurately represent vehicle emissions, and using the dual RS system is essential to identify high-emitters.
the dual RS technique should be used to identify high-emitting vehicles and the single RS technique is sufficient to estimate the average emission factor for a vehicle group.
the single RS technique is more suitable for monitoring and controlling on-road vehicles at the population level, while the dual technique is more suitable at the individual vehicle level.
